ety.text: Borrowed from French véhicule, from Latin vehiculum (“a carriage, conveyance”), from vehō, vehere (“to carry”).

senses.d: A conveyance: a spacious device for carrying or transporting substances, objects, people or animals.
A guided or aimed mobile object or apparatus, especially if intended or used as a weapon.
A medium for expression of talent or views.
ex: supporting actors in a Steven Spielberg vehicle

senses.d: A liquid content (e.g., oil) which acts as a binding and drying agent in paint.
The main excipient (such as an oil or gel) that conveys the active ingredient of a drug.
ex: an ointment with a petrolatum vehicle

senses.d: An entity to achieve an end.
ex: mission service as a vehicle for development of better-rounded worldviews

senses.d: A mode or method of spiritual practice; a yana.
An animal or (rarely) a plant on which a Hindu deity rides or sits.
To transport in a vehicle, or as if in a vehicle.

grp.label: Hinduism: animal or plant on which a Hindu deity sits

chain.g: A means of transport; vehicle, conveyance, carriage; wagon, cart; ship.

pt:veículo.gl: vehicle; conveyance (device for carrying or transporting)

ety.text: Learned borrowing from Latin vehiculum (“vehicle”), from vehō (“to bear, to carry”), from Proto-Indo-European *weǵʰ- (“to ride”).

ety.text: From Old Galician-Portuguese meio, meo, from Latin medius, from Proto-Italic *meðios, from Proto-Indo-European *médʰyos (“between”). Compare the borrowed doublets médio and médium. Sense of "way" or "mean" from Latin medium.
